items.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Lou Levy, the boss of the publishing company, said, 'Toots, you got your foot in the door now, man. Write, write, write, write and bring it to me.'

ctx.x: That’s the best compliment you can get, being called Lady by [Frez?]. [laughs]

Yeah. And in those days, that’s… that was [the start?] of the bus and story, because [Lou Levy?], the owner of [Berlin?], you know, or operator of [inaudible], I don’t know. He was taking care of the music that was also [unintelligible]. [laughs] Smoke material. [laughs] [inaudible]. Let’s move to another chapter.
Well, let’s talk about what made your name among the others as having written a standard—Bluesette. Can you talk about writing Bluesette?
